page: Hetzner Cloud cpx21 is a shared-resource virtual server powered by the QEMU hypervisor on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 3 vCPUs derived from an AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, configured with 1 thread per physical core. The compute configuration is backed by 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 1.3 GB of RAM per vCPU, alongside a 16 MB L3 cache. Local storage is directly integrated into the instance, featuring an 80 GB NVMe SSD. Hardware acceleration via GPUs is not included, and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not provisioned with the base instance.

Benchmark results reflect entry-level compute capability and shared-core characteristics. In stress-ng testing, the instance logged 2667.29 for single-core and 7981.45 for multi-core performance, situating both metrics within the median tier. Geekbench evaluations returned a single-core score of 1469.0 and a multi-core score of 3733.0. In memory and IO-intensive tasks, performance drops into lower tiers; the PassMark memory rating of 1148.15 falls within the bottom decile, while uncached memory bandwidth registers at 37.21 GB/sec for reads and 20.78 GB/sec for writes. Workloads requiring AVX-512 extensions are unsupported on this processor configuration, though standard AVX, AES-NI, and SHA extensions are present.

From an architectural standpoint, the cpx21 maintains a lean resource ratio that favors lightweight computational workloads over memory-heavy or high-throughput enterprise pipelines. The inclusion of bundled NVMe SSD storage offers low-latency local disk access, but throughput remains bound by the 4.0 GB RAM constraint and shared CPU tenancy. The instance is suited for lightweight web serving, utility services, low-concurrency backend tasks, staging environments, and basic automation pipelines.

It delivers 3 shared vCPUs clocked at 2.0 GHz alongside 4.0 GB of RAM, resulting in 1.3 GB of memory per core. Local persistent storage is provisioned via a bundled 80 GB NVMe SSD, while dedicated GPU hardware is absent. Synthetic testing demonstrates mid-tier CPU execution, highlighted by a stress-ng multi-core score of 7981.45 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1469.0. However, memory subsystem benchmarks show constraints, with uncached read throughput measuring 37.21 GB/sec and a PassMark memory score in the bottom decile. Given the 4.0 GB memory envelope and shared compute profile, the cpx21 is positioned for lightweight web servers, background task runners, continuous integration workers, and low-scale application environments.
